messages:
alex: quick heads-up — our eu-west1 dedicated canary pool is showing inter-node stalls after the driver/CUDA push at 09:02 UTC. NCCL allreduce hangs on some H100-backed nodes. logs show repeated timeouts.

maria: ugh. which driver version landed?

alex: 535.22 + CUDA 12.2, applied via the staged-driver-rollout job. only ~6 canary nodes in the pool, 3 of them repro.

jordan: paste of the failing stack from one node: 
```
[2026-03-18T09:15:04Z] nccl: NCCL ERROR Call to cudaLaunchKernel returned 700 (an illegal memory access was encountered)
stack: /opt/nvidia/lib64/libnvidia-ml.so -> /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so
... nvmlDeviceGetVoltage failed ...
```

sam: is this kernel compatibility or driver bug? last regression we saw was a kernel ABI mismatch after a patched kernel. what kernel version on those nodes?

alex: kernel is 5.15.85-rt. Same baseline as other regions where canaries are clean. suspect driver/CUDA combo on H100 microcode.

kai: current customer impact? any Dedicated customers hitting errors?

alex: none reported yet on control plane, but we see elevated job retries and a few capacity errors when autoscaler tries to schedule to those drained nodes. impact is localized to the canary pool but could hit eu-west1 Dedicated if we continue.

ops-bot: ALERT: 3 nodes in eu-west1-dedicated-canary flagged (node-cc-0123, node-cc-0178, node-cc-0246) — nccl errors detected — ticket INF-3427 created.

maria: propose immediate rollback of driver on remaining canaries + pause phased rollout. We should also add a routing rule to avoid eu-west1 for dedicated placements until we know more.

jordan: +1 to pausing. rollback steps: 1) stop staged-driver-rollout job 2) drain affected canaries 3) revert driver to 534.89 on the canary nodes 4) run a small stress test (kv-cache + multi-gpu allreduce) 5) uncordon and monitor 6) decide rollforward.

alex: i'm on 1-3. starting drain on the 3 repro nodes. command: `kubectl drain node-cc-0123 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60`

sam: i'll prepare the revert image and push to infra-registry, tag: `driver-534.89-eu-rollback-20260318`. keep it in canary channel only.

deploy-bot: Rollout job stopped by @maria at 09:28 UTC — canary stop confirmed.

maria: also adding a temporary routing policy to avoid eu-west1 for Dedicated allocations. can someone file a tickets/comms to sales/customer success? we should pre-emptively notify any large reserved customers in eu-west1.

alex: filing INF-3427 with summary + affected nodes + rollback steps. pinging CS @kai for outreach.

kai: on it — i'll DM the top 5 enterprise accounts and draft a short status email. prefer to avoid public incident if we contain it to canaries.

jordan: after revert and stress tests pass, let's run a controlled micro-canary: 2 nodes with driver 534.89, 2 with 535.22 but different kernel (5.19) in a separate pool to isolate kernel interaction. if stable, we can either continue rollout with driver pinned by kernel or engage NVIDIA.

sam: cost note — if we route away from eu-west1 and shift Dedicated traffic to us-west1/eu-central for the week, we should estimate cross-region egress + reserved capacity bump. rough calc: additional $2.1k/day if steady state. flagging to finance for approval if needed.

maria: approved for initial 48h contingency. finance, please prioritize.

ops-bot: INF-3427 updated: rollback initiated, routing policy applied, CS notified.

alex: revert complete on the 3 nodes. running k8s tests now: `make e2e-gpu-test FOCUS=nccl --nodes node-cc-0123,node-cc-0178,node-cc-0246`

jordan: monitoring dashboards — token latency and job retries returning to baseline on those nodes. no new nccl errors in last 12m.

maria: good. leave the phased rollout paused until we confirm across a larger sample. we'll also open an ENG-NVIDIA ticket with logs and kernel details.

sam: creating the ticket now, attaching NVML and dmesg extracts. also adding a small perf harness to compare kernel 5.19 vs 5.15 with 535.22 to reproduce.

kai: CS update sent to the 5 customers. keeping messaging: "no customer-facing downtime, proactive rollback to ensure stability, we'll follow up with root cause." :thumbsup:

alex: plan for tomorrow: 1) reproduce in lab with same microcode 2) if repro, escalate to NVIDIA and pause release indefinitely 3) if no repro, run expanded canary with kernel permutations and extended soak (6h).

maria: agreed. thanks all — nice quick ops here. keep this thread for coordination. I'll close INF-3427 when we have ENG-NVIDIA response or expanded canary results.

jordan: leaving some playbook notes for the runbook: 
```
- Stop staged-driver-rollout job
- Drain repro nodes
- Revert driver image to last-known-good
- Run e2e-gpu-test focusing on nccl
- Apply routing policy to avoid region for Dedicated allocations
- Notify CS and finance for cost/backfill
- Escalate to NVIDIA with logs + kernel/microcode details
```

alex: adding one more: capture nvdisasm output and pci topology for repro nodes.

maria: thanks. closing loop for now.
